title: Early Patna cauliflower: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Early Patna cauliflower: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Early Patna cauliflower is a cauliflower variety. 57 to 63 days to harvest, 6.9 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: Early Patna is a registered cauliflower variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. B.M. Domingo bred it. It takes 57 to 63 days from transplanting to harvest, with 6.93 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 57 to 63 days from transplanting to harvest.
**Yield:** 6.93 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Early Patna cauliflower
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Early Patna cauliflower takes 57 to 63 days from transplanting to harvest. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cauliflower fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Early Patna cauliflower
Cauliflower needs cool nights to form a tight white curd, so it is a highland crop. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 57 to 63 days from transplanting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 6.93 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Early Patna?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
